Resolution through packages/theme/css/next/characteristics/{actionable,container,focused}.css, next/palette/{neutral,accent,foreground,alpha}.css, next/foundations/color.css, packages/theme/css/foundations/{size,spacing,cursor,borderStyle}.css.
provenance.single-select-only-confirmed: ToggleButtonGroup.tsx's `role="radiogroup"` is a hardcoded literal, not conditional on any prop. `isSelected(id) { return value === id }` (ToggleButtonGroupContext.ts, via useToggleButtonGroup) is strict-equality against ONE held `value`. The `Value` type (`string | readonly string[] | number | undefined`) permits an array, but no code path anywhere in ToggleButtonGroup.tsx/ToggleButton.tsx ever compares an array's CONTENTS — a real array value would only match by reference, so multiselect is a type artifact, not a working feature, confirmed by reading every reference to `value`/`isSelected`/`select` in both files.

provenance.selected-hover-scrim: NOT a separate slot — recorded here for provenance completeness. actionable.css --salt-actionable-bold-background-hover: linear-gradient(var(--salt-palette-alpha-dark-low), var(--salt-palette-alpha-dark-low)) var(--salt-palette-neutral) -> alpha-dark-low resolves to black-15a in BOTH modes (alpha.css) -> a darkening scrim OVER the existing --neutral fill, not a flat colour swap. A SELECTED item's hover treatment is therefore mechanically different from an UNSELECTED item's own bg-hover slot — declared in style.item.hover's row note rather than given its own row, matching the scope-control precedent other components use for a secondary variant axis.

This is genuinely a HYBRID, not a clean single-role citation: next/characteristics/text.css's own [data-mode] block resolves --salt-text-action-textTransform to `uppercase` and --salt-text-action-letterSpacing to `0.6px` — a REAL, VISIBLE fact (Salt toggle-button labels render in ALL CAPS with letter-spacing) this column's first draft omitted entirely by only citing font-size/line-height/font-family/font-weight; fixed by adding both to style.root.font's cell.
provenance.no-selected-marker: CONFIRMED ABSENCE — grepped ToggleButton.tsx/ToggleButtonIcon-equivalent (there is none) in full: no glyph/icon/indicator element exists anywhere; the checked/selected signal is entirely a background/foreground/border recolour of the button itself.
provenance.no-transition: CONFIRMED ABSENCE, and it is an EXPLICIT statement not a bare gap: ToggleButton.css's own base rule literally declares `transition: none;`.
provenance.disabled-preserves-selected: ToggleButton.css: `.saltToggleButton[aria-disabled="true"] { background: var(--toggleButton-background); ...; opacity: 0.4 }` (resets to REST/unselected colours) is immediately followed by `.saltToggleButton[aria-checked="true"].saltToggleButton[aria-disabled="true"], .saltToggleButton[aria-pressed="true"].saltToggleButton[aria-disabled="true"] { background: var(--toggleButton-background-selected); ...}` (re-applies SELECTED colours, without re-declaring opacity) — so a disabled+selected item keeps its fill while still dimming via the opacity property alone, confirmed by reading the cascade order directly.
provenance.cursor-hover-equals-cursor-active: foundations/cursor.css: --salt-cursor-hover: pointer; --salt-cursor-active: pointer — two differently-named tokens resolving to the identical CSS keyword, confirmed directly.
